title: Will make you cry and want to call your parents #picturesfromhome #br...
transcript: I went to go see Pictures from Home, a new play that is currently playing on Broadway at Studio 54. and I knew literally nothing about this show going in except the cast. the plot is very simple. it follows the photographer Larry Sultan and this project that he released in the 90s where he took photographs of his parents for years. and the play is a really interesting exploration, not just with his relationship with his parents, but also just our relationship with art and creating art. and how much of real life can you capture in something like a photograph? I consider this to be a very slice of life, low stakes show, but I found it really moving. this play kind of took me by surprise, mostly because I literally knew nothing about it going in, but I really enjoyed it. the entire cast is obviously fantastic. very much put this in the same realm as Birthday Candles. it's a play that I really, really loved and enjoyed. I don't think it's going to win or maybe even be nominated for any Tony Awards in such a strong season, but I definitely think it's still worth seeing. I also think it's interesting that this was pretty used in the same season as Death of a Salesman. I think that they have a lot of similarities. um, just one is very dramatic and shows kind of like, the anguish of mediocrity, and this one kind of embraces it. overall, I really enjoyed this play, and honestly, out of all the plays currently on Broadway, this is my favorite until like March.
